# dsh-terminal-vision
**Terminal semantic vision plugin for DeepSeek Harness (DSH).**
Gives the agent "semantic vision" over interactive terminal programs — vim, htop, lazygit, less, set
up TUIs — instead of a raw escape-sequence byte stream. Every PTY session is continuously parsed by
@xterm/headless (the headless JS port of xterm.js) into a structured **screen model**: visible text
lines, cursor position, active line. The agent can then *read the screen*, *send keys*, *read again*
— a perception/action loop over any TUI.
## Tools registered in DSH
| Tool | Purpose |
| `terminal_open(session_name, shell?, cwd?, cols?, rows?)` | Open a persistent PTY session, returns
`session_id`. `shell` may be a shell name (`bash`, `pwsh`, `cmd`) **or** a TUI program to run direc

tly (`htop`, `vim file.txt`). |
| `terminal_get_screen(session_id)` | Structured screen model: `line

s[]`, `cursor {x, y}`, `active_line`, terminal title. |
| `terminal_send_keys(session_id, keys, wait
_ms?)` | Send a key sequence and **wait for the screen to change** (readiness wait, default 500 ms),
then return the new screen. Accepts plain text, named keys (`Enter`, `Esc`, `Up`…), modifiers (`Ctr

l+C`, `Alt+b`), space-separated sequences (`":wq Enter"`). |
| `terminal_read_output(session_id, lin

es?)` | Last N lines of the scrollback buffer (history above the viewport). |
| `terminal_close(sess

ion_id)` | Close the session and free the PTY. |
| `terminal_list_sessions()` | List active sessions
with id, name, shell, cwd, alive status. |
## Architecture
- **Host part (TypeScript, `src/`)** — Cordis plugin: `apply(ctx)` registers the tools on `ctx.tools
`, manages persistent sessions via **node-pty** (prebuilt ConPTY binaries on Windows — no compiler n

eeded).
- **Semantic parser (`src/screen-model.ts`)** — **Variant A**: `@xterm/headless` builds the
screen model natively in Node. Raw PTY output is written into a headless xterm Terminal; the buffer
is read out on demand (`buffer.active`, `translateToString`). No Python, no long-lived bridge proces

s, works offline.
- Keys are translated by `encodeKeys()` (friendly names → terminal bytes, includin

g Ctrl/Alt modifiers, arrows, F-keys).
- Readiness wait: after each `terminal_send_keys`, the tool w
aits until the screen revision changes (data arrives) or the timeout elapses — preventing "blind" se

nds.
- All tools return JSON-serializable objects; unknown session ids return a clear error instead
ools return JSON-serializable objects; unknown session ids return a clear error instead of crashing.

## Build & test (development)
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`lib/` (compiled JS) is committed, so a plain `dsh plugin add` needs no build step. For the same rea
son the package deliberately has **no `prepare` script**: pnpm blocks git-hosted packages from runni
ng build scripts on install (`ERR_PNPM_GIT_DEP_PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED`), and since `lib/` is already in
the repository the build is unnecessary. When developing, run `npm run build` and commit the update
sitory the build is unnecessary. When developing, run `npm run build` and commit the updated `lib/`.
## Dependencies

- **Node.js >= 22.19** (DSH host requirement)
- `node-pty` ^1.1.0 — ships prebuilt Windows ConPTY bi

naries; no Visual Studio Build Tools required on Windows 11
- `@xterm/headless` ^6.0.0 — pure JS, no

native code
- No Python, no root/admin rights
## Known limitations
- The screen model is text-only: colors/attributes are parsed by the emulator but not exposed in the

snapshot.
- `cursorHidden` is advisory (xterm.js does not expose the DECTCEM state); most TUIs keep

the cursor visible.
- `Alt+<letter>` sends ESC-prefixed bytes (application keypad mode not negotiat

ed per-program).
- Sessions live in the DSH host process; restarting DSH closes all sessions.
- On W
indows the default shell is `cmd.exe` (ConPTY); `bash` works if Git Bash / WSL bash is on PATH.
